stated: Make misogyny a hate crime and give police and prosecutors the resources and training they need to prevent and prosecute all hate crimes while supporting survivors.

source.quote: Make misogyny a hate crime and give police and prosecutors the resources and training they need to prevent and prosecute all hate crimes while supporting survivors.

bearing_set.reason: Criminalising misogyny as a hate crime directly affects how crimes are categorised, investigated, and prosecuted, plus resources/training for police and prosecutors — squarely a crime, policing and justice-system measure.
Extending hate-crime status to misogyny is a legal equal-treatment and anti-discrimination reform, creating formal parity of protection for women — directly within the rights/freedoms scope.

Criminalising misogyny as a hate crime can restrict currently lawful expression, creating a concrete chilling-effect mechanism on free speech and a new category of state coercion over conduct and communication.

membership_note: Three fundamentals bear materially: O5 (safety/justice effect of expanded hate crime law), O9 (equal-treatment extension to women), and O10 (liberty cost via criminalisation of expression). The stated resource commitment to police/prosecutors is too small in absolute terms to move the macro debt path materially (O12 excluded). O15 cohesion effects are plausible but indirect and secondary to the three identified bearings.
